hyperedges.description: The three-link stealth chain (transport identity via wreq-util/resolve, JS fingerprint injection via profiles.ts, and capture verification via tools/capture) plus the load_all() loader that reads captured JSON definitions, together restore consistent browser-identity spoofing across transport and JS layers.
Scrape and Parse share one response envelope (Document/ParseDocument) and both drive structured extraction through ExtractConfig-shaped jsonOptions using the operator's configured LLM.

The /app/agent UI posts a prompt through the dashboard's agent route to apps/api's agent.ts, which calls ExtractClient.schema against helix-extract's schema_gen.py, implementing the /agent/schema OpenAPI operation end to end.

nodes.label: Why the min-h-full Wrapper Attempt Failed
nodes.norm_label: why the min-h-full wrapper attempt failed
nodes.rationale: A min-h-full wrapper around children placed the absolutely positioned grid above any page whose root was not positioned, because absolute siblings paint over unpositioned in-flow content regardless of DOM order; this also broke PageFrame's own min-h-full so the overview's column borders stopped at content bottom. Fixed by making the grid sticky top-0 z-[-1] h-0 inside an isolate, [container-type:size] main sized h-[100cqh]: sticky with zero height takes no space, cqh sizes to the scroll area rather than the viewport, and z-[-1] inside isolate paints below in-flow content.

nodes.rationale: Animation should explain the ladder mechanic, not decorate around it — no competitor surfaces escalation reasoning.

nodes.label: Escalation policy (content-presence test)
nodes.rationale: Content-presence in raw HTML triggers escalation, not framework name — Next.js/Nuxt often server-render real content, so escalating on framework alone burns the expensive tier for nothing.

nodes.label: Fetch ladder (4 tiers)
nodes.rationale: Cheapest first: tier0 plain HTTP ~5ms, tier1 TLS-impersonating ~50ms, tier2 Lightpanda ~25ms, tier3 Chromium ~2-5s. Escalate only on evidence, never a framework guess.

nodes.label: prefers-reduced-motion rule
nodes.rationale: Reduced motion removes cycling, never the information — settled frame renders immediately since every frame is a legible state diagram.

nodes.label: Tier colour scale by value not hue
nodes.norm_label: tier colour scale by value not hue
nodes.rationale: The mark's own descent bright violet to near-black reused so the ladder reads as one family getting heavier as it gets more expensive; four hues would compete with the logo.

hyperedges.description: The three-link stealth chain (transport identity via wreq-util/resolve, JS fingerprint injection via profiles.ts, and capture verification via tools/capture) plus the load_all() loader that reads captured JSON definitions, together restore consistent browser-identity spoofing across transport and JS layers.
Scrape and Parse share one response envelope (Document/ParseDocument) and both drive structured extraction through ExtractConfig-shaped jsonOptions using the operator's configured LLM.

The /app/agent UI posts a prompt through the dashboard's agent route to apps/api's agent.ts, which calls ExtractClient.schema against helix-extract's schema_gen.py, implementing the /agent/schema OpenAPI operation end to end.
